hypotheses.name: live is numerically the realized-trajectory gradient where the champion is stable
hypotheses.prediction: pooled over non-diverged cells, the median per-step relative difference between the live and snapshot update vectors is <= 0.001 and its 99th percentile <= 0.01
hypotheses.statement: on cells where the live champion does not diverge, the stale recurrent matrices change the update negligibly: the live update is the snapshot update to within numerical noise

hypotheses.contradicted_by: the snapshot rule diverging in >= 50% as many long coarse cells
hypotheses.name: the stale-matrix mismatch drives M2
hypotheses.prediction: the snapshot rule diverges in <= 20% as many long coarse cells as the live rule
hypotheses.statement: backpropagating old activations through current matrices produces a biased update that feeds the long-horizon runaway

hypotheses.contradicted_by: the T=1 rule diverging in <= 20% as many long coarse cells
hypotheses.name: M2 does not need multi-step credit assignment
hypotheses.prediction: the T=1 rule diverges in >= 50% as many long coarse cells as the live rule
hypotheses.statement: the runaway arises in the one-step update; truncated backpropagation beyond it is not required

hypotheses.contradicted_by: the replay rule diverging in >= 50% as many long coarse cells
hypotheses.name: chunk-consistent credit prevents M2
hypotheses.prediction: the replay rule diverges in <= 20% as many long coarse cells as the live rule
hypotheses.statement: gradients recomputed under one parameter value across the window (constant-parameter chunked TBPTT) remove the runaway
